topics.topic: Enforcement and failure handling for deterministic function execution
questions: What rule detects or prevents outputs that vary despite passing all listed sandbox traps?
What happens when the same implementation and inputs produce different valid outputs, and what mechanism makes the claimed determinism enforceable?
Which observable sources must be blocked or fixed so deterministic execution is enforceable, and what outcome is recorded when code accesses one?

judgement.why: This asks the same deterministic-execution enforcement question already judged in P3, and its quoted requirement remains unchanged.

precedent.topic: Definition and enforcement of deterministic function execution
quotes: The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.
precedent.why: The determinism requirement and its enforcement question predated the change and were untouched by it.

topics.topic: Exact runtime, tool, and dependency versions defining release v1
questions: Which exact CPython, bubblewrap and kernel dependency versions define release v1?
What exact dependency and tool versions constitute release v1, including the required `bubblewrap`, SQLite binding/runtime, HTTP client, MCP stack, and schema validator?
What exact CPython patch version, bubblewrap version range, HTTP/TLS stack and other dependency versions define release v1 behavior?

judgement.why: This is the same release-v1 runtime and dependency version question judged in P21.

precedent.topic: Exact interpreter, runtime, dependency, and sandbox versions defining release v1
quotes:
A release pins the exact versions of the kernel's Python dependencies and of
   the sandbox runtime (A03); the sandbox interpreter of release v1 is CPython
   3.12, whose `random` module gives A03 rule 4 its list.
precedent.why: The runtime-version passage was unchanged, and the reopening change did not make the missing patch, build, dependency or bubblewrap versions matter.

topics.topic: Permitted filesystem access for sandboxed function code
questions: May function code read runtime files or create/read arbitrary exchange-directory files, or may it access only its supplied inputs and declared outputs?
May function code read arbitrary files from the runtime and create or read scratch files in the exchange directory, or must filesystem access be limited to kernel-provided input and output paths?
May agent code inspect the runtime, enumerate or read exchange files, and create arbitrary scratch files, or must filesystem access be limited to runner-managed input and output objects?

judgement.why: This is the same sandbox filesystem-access question judged in P5, based on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Function filesystem access inside the sandbox and exchange directory
quotes:
A function node runs one admitted implementation of one contract: declared input
in, declared output out, no network, no filesystem beyond its input, no clock, no
randomness, no secret, no service handle.
precedent.why: The filesystem restriction was unchanged, and the change did not alter sandbox path access.

topics.topic: Retention and cleanup of unpublished files from failed or oversized attempts
questions: Are bytes from an oversized or otherwise failed output physically removed immediately, retained unnamed until spool cleanup, or retained only for some failure classes?
Are bytes from a failed or oversized attempt removed immediately, or retained as unnamed spool files until run cleanup?
Are unpublished files from a failed or oversized attempt physically removed immediately, retained unnamed until run cleanup, or handled differently for per-file and per-run ceiling failures?

quotes:
the files its attempt spooled are discarded with no
   SpooledFile record naming them: no operation removes them at once — they stay
   in the run's spool, counted toward `spool_run_bytes_max`, until that spool is
   removed

A function writing a file one byte over `spool_file_bytes_max` concludes
   `resource_exhausted` and leaves nothing in the spool.
judgement.why: One passage retains unnamed failed-attempt files until spool removal, while the required test says an oversized file leaves nothing in the spool.

topics.topic: Valid service base URLs and deterministic joining with operation paths
questions: Which path, query, fragment, user-information, percent-encoding and port forms are legal in api_base_url, and exactly how are they joined to the declared path?
What exact forms of `api_base_url` are valid, and exactly how is its path joined to the operation path?

Are user-info, a query, a fragment, multiple trailing slashes, a non-root base path, Unicode host names and explicit default ports allowed, and exactly how are they joined and represented in the request and approval digest?

judgement.why: This is the same base-URL grammar and operation-path joining question judged in P1.

precedent.topic: Accepted api_base_url grammar and operation-path joining
precedent.why: The accepted base-URL grammar, joining rules and Host serialization are format and encoding details belonging to State 6.

topics.topic: Validation, escaping, and wire serialization of multipart requests
questions: Which port names are valid for multipart bindings, and how are quotes, backslashes, non-ASCII characters or control characters encoded or refused?
Which port names are valid in multipart headers, how are quoted parameters escaped, and how is the boundary and complete multipart body serialized?
What lexical rules or escaping apply to port names, filenames and media types before they are inserted into multipart headers?

judgement.why: This is the same multipart field-name, escaping, boundary and serialization question judged in P49.

precedent.topic: Canonical multipart serialization, field-name encoding, and approval identity
precedent.why: Multipart wire serialization, escaping, boundary generation and request-description encoding are State 6 format and encoding matters.

topics.topic: Canonical ordering of tied edges and constants for identity and proof checks
questions: How are tied edges or constants ordered before hashing so that reordering semantically identical content cannot change `flow_version_id`?
How are tied edges and constants ordered for canonical identity and for selecting the first proof failure?

judgement.why: This is the same missing tie-breaker question for canonical edge and constant ordering judged in P20.

precedent.topic: Canonical ordering and first-failure order for tied flow edges and constants
quotes:
Lists
   whose order carries no meaning are sorted before hashing — ports by
   (`direction`, `name`), nodes by `node_id`, edges in the edge order of A05,
   constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`) — so the same content in another order has
   the same identity; list values themselves keep their order.
precedent.why: The missing tie-breakers were already present in the unchanged identity-ordering rule.

topics.topic: Capture, limits, and failure behavior for sandbox stdout and stderr
questions: Are stdout and stderr discarded continuously, bounded as output or scratch, or allowed to block the process and cause a timeout?
Are stdout and stderr discarded, bounded, or allowed to block, and which execution outcome results when their limit is exceeded?

quotes:
Nothing the code prints or raises is interpreted by the kernel. The kernel keeps
   at most `failure_detail_bytes_max` of it as `failure_detail`, and only for the
   exception type and message, never stdout.
judgement.why: The destination, draining and limiting of stdout and stderr were already unspecified by this unchanged passage, and the reopening change did not make them matter.

topics.topic: Contract-port validation rules and ordering for operation bindings
questions: Which contract-port validity rules apply to binding ports, including supported-schema validation, disclosure-class placement, and whether at least one output is required?
Must a binding proposal be refused when one of its port schemas is outside the supported JSON Schema subset, and where does that check occur in the mismatch order?

judgement.why: This is the same binding-port schema admissibility and validation question judged in P18.

precedent.topic: Admissibility and validation order of schemas on bindings, flow ports, and constants
quotes:
Any other keyword —
   `$ref`, `pattern`, `format`, `oneOf`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, `not` among them —
   is outside the subset: A02 refuses it in a contract version, and
   `fit_port_value` answers that no value fits it, so a binding or flow port
   written outside the subset can never deliver.
precedent.why: State 6 specifies that contracts refuse unsupported schemas while binding and flow ports may contain them but can never deliver a fitting value.

topics.topic: Host forms and DNS behavior qualifying for the plain-HTTP loopback exception
questions: What exact host representations qualify for the loopback exception, and how are DNS changes or multiple resolved addresses handled?
Do `localhost`, IPv4-mapped IPv6, alternate numeric IPv4 spellings, or a hostname resolving to loopback qualify?

judgement.why: This is the same plain-HTTP loopback qualification and DNS question judged in P7.

precedent.topic: Qualification and DNS handling for the plain-HTTP loopback exception
quotes:
Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
precedent.why: The definition of loopback concerns unchanged text and was not made material by the change.

topics.topic: Input references recorded on mapped-node aggregate failure traces
questions: What exact input references does the aggregate no-map_index NodeExecution contain for the mapped port and for shared ports?
Does that aggregate record name the original mapped list and shared inputs, every element's per-call inputs, only the inputs of the first failing output port, or another representation?

judgement.divergence: One implementer records the original mapped list plus the shared inputs as one PortRef per port; another records per-element input references or omits inputs that cannot fit that shape. Owners and agents reading the aggregate failure trace observe different input provenance.
judgement.why: Neither State 2 nor the later texts define the aggregate record's input references even though the changed rule requires it to name the inputs the elements received.

topics.topic: Loading, validation, and change semantics of the configured manifest revision
questions: How is manifest_revision applied, and what happens if files at manifest_location change while the configured revision and running process do not?
Does an invalid or unavailable `manifest_revision` stop kernel startup, or does each binding operation fail as though its service record were absent?

judgement.why: This is the same configured-manifest-revision resolution and startup handling question judged in P15.

precedent.topic: Mechanism for resolving and reading a manifest revision
quotes:
**The manifest at a revision**: `manifest_location` is a directory inside a
   git repository and `manifest_revision` a commit of it; `bindings` reads
   `<service_id>.json` of that directory at that commit as a git object, never
   from the working tree, so a record changes only with the configured revision
   (A08 rules 1 and 6).

**A manifest that cannot be read at start** in
   `bindings.check_installed_instances`: the start stops and names it; every
   start step is required (State 3, "Start").
precedent.why: The later text defines revision reads as Git-object reads at a commit and makes an unreadable startup manifest stop startup.

topics.topic: Outcome classification for incomplete or malformed HTTP response bodies
questions: If a valid 2xx status and headers arrive but the body times out, resets or ends before its declared framing completes, is that an unknown transport outcome or an applied contract violation?
After a final status line is received, does an incomplete or malformed body retain the status-based outcome or count as no valid final response?

judgement.why: This is the same response-interruption classification question judged in P10.

precedent.topic: Classification of a response interrupted after final status and headers
quotes: send_prepared_request: [BEHAVIOR] The outcome is decided in this order, with effect_class read meaning the read column: a failure of name resolution, connection or TLS before the first request byte was written is service_unreachable, attempt not_sent for other classes; a timeout, reset, end of stream, malformed status line or headers — a status line and header section longer together than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant included —, or only 1xx after the first byte was written is service_unreachable for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 3xx is operation_failed with detail redirect_not_followed for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 5xx is service_unreachable for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 4xx is operation_refused, attempt not_applied for other classes; 2xx whose body as read contains the bytes of the credential value sent, searched before parsing, or whose outputs do not fit is contract_violation, attempt applied for other classes; 2xx whose outputs fit is succeeded, attempt applied for other classes.
precedent.why: The later invoker contract gives timeout, reset or end-of-stream precedence after any request byte was written, producing unknown for non-read effects.

topics.topic: Ownership, permissions, links, and file types required for data-directory privacy
questions: What exact filesystem ownership and permission conditions must every directory and file satisfy at startup?
Which owner, mode, parent-directory, hard-link and file-type conditions make the data directory and each contained object private?

judgement.why: This is the same data-directory ownership and permission question judged in P16.

precedent.topic: Ownership, file-type, and permission requirements for private installation data
quotes:
The directory and everything in it
   are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
precedent.why: The exact meaning of private filesystem state was already unspecified in this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: Representation and derivation of aggregate disclosure classes for file lists
questions: Where is a file list's aggregate disclosure class recorded or deterministically derived, especially for an empty list after restart?
Where is the aggregate list class represented, and which class controls disclosure when individual file classes differ or the list is empty?

judgement.why: This is the same durable representation of aggregate many-file disclosure classes judged in P30.

precedent.topic: Durable identity and disclosure class of many-file outputs, including empty lists
quotes:
`SpooledFilesRef`
    gains `disclosure_class`, the class of the file list it names, so an empty
    list keeps the class A13 rule 6 gives it and counts in an execution's
    class (A07 rule 5).
precedent.why: The later contract explicitly stores the class on the file-list reference, including an empty list.

topics.topic: Required completeness of authored trial inputs and expected outputs
questions: May an authored case assert only a subset of outputs, or must expected_outputs be either wholly absent or exactly match all contract outputs?
Must trial inputs contain exactly every input port, and, when `expected_outputs` is present, must it contain exactly every output port?

judgement.why: This is the same required completeness of trial input and expected-output maps judged in P22.

precedent.topic: Required completeness and exactness of authored trial input and expected-output maps
precedent.why: Required and optional request fields and the exact trial-case input and expected-output shapes belong to State 6 schemas.

topics.topic: Scope of stored-value size limits for JSON service responses
questions: Is stored_value_bytes_max enforced on the whole JSON response body, on each output member separately, or both?
For a JSON response with several output members, does `stored_value_bytes_max` constrain the whole response body, each output value separately, or both?

quotes: | status 2xx, the body echoes the credential (rule 7), outputs do not fit rule 3, or the body exceeds `service_response_bytes_max`, `stored_value_bytes_max` or the spool ceilings | `contract_violation` | `contract_violation`, attempt `applied` |

A value a node produces — a function output or a service output — above
   `stored_value_bytes_max` is checked only after the execution or the response
   has otherwise succeeded, so A03's `resource_exhausted` for `output_bytes` wins
   when both hold; it concludes the element `contract_violation` with detail
   `value_too_large`;
judgement.why: A09 applies the stored-value ceiling to the response body, while A15 applies it to each service output value.

topics.topic: Valid manifest record shapes and classification order for malformed records
questions: What complete manifest shape is required, and where do each of these malformed structures fall in the ordered manifest-mismatch checks?
What exact manifest shapes are valid, how are all malformed shapes classified, and where do their failures fall in rule 5's first-failure order?

judgement.why: This is the same manifest schema and malformed-record failure-order question judged in P9.

precedent.topic: Accepted manifest schema and ordering of malformed-document failures
precedent.why: The exact manifest schema, nested field types and malformed-shape validation belong to State 6.

topics.topic: Whether multipart boundary changes invalidate an approval
questions: Do changes in multipart boundary and resulting wire body or Content-Length invalidate an approval?
Does a changed multipart boundary invalidate an approval, or is the boundary explicitly outside the approved request identity?

quotes:
the
    fully built request as the owner was shown it — method, URL, headers and
    body. Any difference at send, whatever caused it (the inputs, or an
    instance's address or headers changed by a restart), asks again.

The body is described as the JSON body's bytes, or for
   `multipart/form-data` as the parts in order, each as its name, filename when
   present, media type and the SHA-256 of its content, so the boundary is not
   part of it: equal parts give equal descriptions.
judgement.why: State 0 says any difference in the fully built request body asks again, while A10 expressly excludes the multipart boundary from request identity.

topics.topic: Accounting scope of sandbox memory and process-count limits
questions: What exactly is counted against `memory_bytes` and `process_count` for the whole sandbox execution?

topics.topic: Addressing and disambiguation of flow endpoints and empty node identifiers
questions: May a node have the empty identifier, and how are flow-input and flow-output endpoints distinguished from each other and from such a node?

topics.topic: Allowed HTTP header-value characters and their wire encoding
questions: Which characters are permitted in header values, how are they encoded on the wire, and do C1 controls, DEL, tabs, leading spaces or non-ASCII text cause refusal?

topics.topic: Byte serialization of string and integer HTTP path placeholders
questions: What exact bytes are placed into the URL for string and integer path values?

topics.topic: Canonical value and field ordering used for effect idempotency-key hashing
questions: What exact JSON value is hashed for one or several idempotency-key fields, and how are field names and manifest field order represented?

topics.topic: Classification of a selected service instance missing from the manifest
questions: Is a selected name missing from the manifest `instance_not_selected`, `instance_address_missing`, a manifest mismatch, or a startup configuration error?

topics.topic: Disclosure class of outputs from a no-input trial
questions: What disclosure class does an expected output or trial execution output have for a function contract with no inputs?

topics.topic: Durable identification of the activation authorizing draft-write sends
questions: How does a run durably identify which activation authorized its draft-write sends when the same flow version has been activated more than once?

topics.topic: Equality semantics used when evaluating guards
questions: Is guard equality canonical-JSON byte equality, JSON structural equality, or language-native equality, particularly for numbers such as `1` and `1.0`?

topics.topic: Evidence and precedence used to classify sandbox resource exhaustion
questions: What observable evidence makes an abnormal termination resource_exhausted rather than crashed when several limits or signals could explain it?

topics.topic: Files and metadata counted toward the sandbox scratch limit
questions: Do staged inputs, runner protocol files, temporary user files, declared outputs, deleted files and filesystem metadata count toward the scratch limit, and how is an exceedance detected?

topics.topic: First-failure ordering when multiple contract ports are invalid
questions: When several ports fail the same condition, including equal names in opposite directions, which port is reported first?

topics.topic: Handling of content-encoded HTTP responses for decoding and limits
questions: Are content-encoded responses rejected, decoded, or treated as their encoded bytes, and which bytes count toward limits and credential-echo detection?

topics.topic: Independent observability of the function-side spool-file size limit
questions: How can the function-side spool_file_bytes_max behavior be observed independently of the lower mandatory output_bytes ceiling?

topics.topic: NodeExecution statuses and conclusion semantics that permit retries
questions: Which NodeExecution statuses leave an element retryable, and does “concluded” mean a concluded attempt or a final element conclusion?

topics.topic: Objects counted toward output size and handling of non-canonical values
questions: Which returned objects count toward output_bytes, and what outcome applies when their size cannot be canonically computed?

topics.topic: Outcome precedence when sandbox cleanup cannot be confirmed after another failure
questions: If an execution times out or exhausts a resource and cleanup then cannot be confirmed, is its recorded outcome the earlier resource outcome or `crashed/cleanup_failed`?

topics.topic: Refusal precedence when a changed proposed binding has multiple validation failures
questions: When the pinned digest differs and the current operation or instance also fails another validation, which refusal is reported first?

topics.topic: Retry policy for rereading an unchanged invalid token configuration
questions: After one invalid reread, is the same unchanged file re-read on every request, or only after its bytes change again?

topics.topic: Semantics of standing grants that name function nodes
questions: Is a grant request naming a function node refused, accepted but unused, or interpreted as a read-class node?

topics.topic: Size limits and failure stages for manifest and instance data
questions: What limits apply to manifest and instance data, and does exceeding one refuse startup, refuse a proposal, or fail an invocation?

topics.topic: Transport evidence and classification for whether request bytes reached the network
questions: What transport observation proves that zero request bytes reached the network, especially through TLS and buffered HTTP clients, and what classification is used when the client cannot expose that fact?

topics.topic: Treatment of undeclared clock and time-observation APIs
questions: Are unlisted clock or time-observation APIs allowed, trapped, or grounds for a sandbox violation when used?

topics.topic: Unit and stage used to measure redacted failure-detail length
questions: Is the disclosed length measured in Unicode characters, UTF-8 bytes before truncation, UTF-8 bytes after truncation, or the original unbounded diagnostic length?

topics.topic: Validation scope of configuration during token hot reload
questions: During token reload, must the entire configuration satisfy its schema, or are non-token fields ignored even when malformed or changed?

topics.topic: Whether independent ready work advances during startup recovery with waiting work
questions: After restart, must ready independent work advance in a run that also has approval, unreachable-service, or unknown-outcome waiting points?

topics.topic: Which prior implementations are eligible for rollback
questions: Which admitted implementations qualify as earlier: any implementation other than the current one, one submitted before the current implementation, or only one previously activated before the current activation?
